newsitem.title: UK: Blair says would appoint British "drug Czar".
newsitem.headline: Blair says would appoint British "drug Czar".

text.p: Labour leader Tony Blair said on Tuesday that if he becomes prime minister, he will appoint a high-powered "drug Czar" to spearhead the fight against illegal drug use.
Speaking in Aberdeen, Scotland, Blair admitted he had borrowed the idea from the United States, where, he said, "such a figure has had substantial success".
"We can do the same here and so help to avoid Britain becoming as scarred by drugs as the US has been," he said.
"I want this person to take a cool hard look at the present operation, and urgently draw up a strategy to tackle drugs with renewed vigour," he added.

He said the "drug Czar" would report directly to a committee headed by a cabinet minister, and would have power to coordinate the work of relevant authorities such as the police, social services, prisons and the probation service.
"This appointment will be a clear manifesto commitment. It will be a valuable added weapon against one of the great evils of our time," Blair said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
